task.title: Harden Windows settings atomic replacement retries
task.objective: Harden the main-process ui-settings atomic replacement path against bounded transient Windows EPERM/EBUSY failures without changing the persisted settings schema, IPC contract, or serial write ordering.

architecture: Do not change the persisted ui-settings schema.
Do not change the IPC contract or window.playwrightFlowStudio surface.
Do not change serial write ordering - the settings queue stays a single FIFO chain.
Retry belongs in an isolated, directly testable helper rather than inline in writeSettings.
compatibility: An existing ui-settings.json must remain readable and untouched when replacement ultimately fails.
flushSettingsWrites() must continue never to reject, so before-quit cannot deadlock.
offline: No new dependency; Node built-ins only.

acceptance.description: Atomic replacement retries ONLY transient EPERM/EBUSY, and only a bounded number of times. A non-transient error is rethrown on the first attempt.
Concurrent independent settings patches remain serialized and lossless; retry delay never lets a later write overtake an earlier one.
Persistent replacement failure propagates to the caller with the prior target file intact and unmodified.
Temporary files are removed on every failure path, including after exhausting retries.
before-quit flush behaviour is unchanged: flushSettingsWrites() still never rejects.

evidence.artifact: 3/3 real-Electron checks: 40 concurrent patches lossless, 0 temp files, flush-on-quit

completion_notes: QC review: retry set is narrow (EPERM/EBUSY only) and proven non-vacuous in both directions; bounded attempts proven by count; original errno preserved; temp cleanup and prior-target integrity driven against a real filesystem; serial ordering preserved under retry. Schema, IPC and queue semantics unchanged.
